lines.label: B1
lines.reason: Plate (2) to back flange (3), 90.1 deg. Sections at 25/50/75% put the line on the outer-skin apex (outer surface along the bisector at +0.01/+0.01/+0.02 mm). The dense 26-station check stays at or below 0.15 mm. The connected fold (inner fillet present) runs from u about -28 to +21.5, and the line runs from -28.2 to 21.8, so it covers the whole fold up to both box corners. The extruded holes in the flange are not bends.

lines.label: B2
lines.reason: Plate (2) to right flange (4), 91.4 deg. Sections at 25/50/75% are on the outer apex (0.01/0.01/0.02 mm). The connected fold runs from v about -25 to +21. Past v=-25 a bend-relief slot separates the flange from the plate (a 0.7 mm gap shows in the sections). The line starts at -27.74, so it overshoots about 2.7 mm into the relief, where it sits 0.6-0.7 mm off the plate edge. That is still within 1 mm, and the line covers about 99% of the fold, so it passes. It is a minor overshoot only.

lines.label: B3
lines.reason: Plate (2) to left flange (7), 90.4 deg. Sections at 25/50/75% are on the outer apex (-0.01/0.00/+0.02 mm). The connected fold runs from v about -3 to +21, with the relief slot beyond -3. The line spans -4.46 to 20.36: it overshoots about 1.5 mm into the relief (up to 0.65 mm off the surface) and stops about 0.6 mm short at the box corner. It covers about 97% of the fold.

lines.label: B4
lines.reason: Plate (2) to notch-edge flange (10), 89.4 deg. Sections at 25/50/75% are on the outer apex (0.03/0.01/0.00 mm), with a dense maximum of 0.08 mm. The fold is connected from v -37.5 to -16, and the line runs from -37.11 to -16.22, covering the full fold. Flange 10 is flat along its length (tilt 0.0-0.3 deg).

missing_bends: LEFT flange (patch 7, the B3 side) free tab end, beyond the bend-relief slot. The tab has a fold about a vertical axis (perpendicular to the plate) between the main flange face and a flat end facet about 2.5 mm long. Fitted planes give 11.3 deg on the outer skin and 10.6 deg on the inner skin (plane rms 0.004-0.010 mm). The transition is about 3 mm long, centred at v=-4.0 in the auditor frame. The tab bends inward, so the outer (convex) apex is on the flange outer face. Approximate outer-apex line in raw source_ply coords: [-148.94,-78.61,152.16] -> [-150.12,-72.71,145.48], running the full tab height (about 9 mm). The initial label excluded this as a 'gentle ~10 deg splay (<15 deg)'. That reason no longer applies under the 10-deg owner rule. It is not a rolled surface: there are two distinct flats with a crease between them. BORDERLINE, at about 0.5-1.3 deg over the threshold.

RIGHT flange (patch 4, the B2 side) free tab end, beyond the relief slot. It mirrors the left-tab kink: 10.5 deg on the outer skin and 10.0 deg on the inner skin between the main flange face and a flat end facet about 2 mm long, centred at v=-27.0. Approximate outer-apex line in raw source_ply coords: [-90.32,-71.63,147.95] -> [-91.50,-65.73,141.26], running the full tab height. The two tabs are symmetric with identical angles and flat facets, so this looks like a deliberately formed lead-in, not damage. BORDERLINE, at 0.0-0.5 deg over the 10 deg threshold. If the owner treats this as a gentle kink, drop both.
